questions.solution:
Number of radial nodes $=n-1-1$
For $3 s$, radial nodes $=3-0-1=2$
For $2 p$, radial nodes $=2-1-1=0$
Hence, the number of radial nodes are 2 , and 0 respectively.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The position of both, an electron and a helium atom is known within $1.0 \mathrm{ nm}$. Further the momentum of the electron is known within 5.0 $\times 10^{-26} \mathrm{ kg} \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$. The minimum uncertainty in the measurement of the momentum of the helium atom is
questions.solution:
By Heisenberg uncertainty Principle
$\Delta x \times \Delta p=\frac{h}{4 \pi}$ (which is constant)
As $\Delta \mathrm{x}$ for electron and helium atom is same thus momentum of electron and helium will also be same therefore the momentum of helium atom is equal to $5 \times 10^{-26} \mathrm{ kg}$. m. $\mathrms^{-1}$.

questions.q: The energies $E_{1}$ and $E_{2}$ of two radiations are 25 $\mathrm{eV}$ and $50 \mathrm{eV}$, respectively. The relation between their wavelengths i.e., $\lambda_{1}$ and $\lambda_{2}$ will be :
questions.solution: Given $E_{1}=25 \mathrm{eV} E_{2}=50 \mathrm{eV} \begin{array}{l}$ E_{1}=$\frac{h c}{\lambda_{1}}$ E_{2}=$\frac{h c}{\lambda_{2}} \therefore \frac{E_{1}}{E_{2}}=\frac{\lambda_{2}}{\lambda_{1}}$\\ \therefore $\frac{\lambda_{2}}{\lambda_{1}}=\frac{25}{50}=\frac{1}{2} \quad \therefore \lambda_{1}=2 \lambda_{2} \end{array} $

questions.q: The ratio of slopes of $K_{\max }$ vs $V and V_{0}$ vs $v$ curves in the photoelectric effects gives $\left(v=\right.$ frequency,$K_{\max }=$ maximum kinetic energy, $v_{0}=$ stopping potential )
options: the ratio of Planck's constant of electronic charge
questions.solution: $\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{hv}=\mathrm{hv}_{0}+\mathrm{ev}_{0} \\ \mathrm{v}_{0}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{v}-\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{v}_{0} \end{array} On comparing this equation with the straight line equation, i.e \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{mx}+\mathrm{c} The slope of \mathrm{v}_{0} vs \mathrm{v}$ is ( $v_{0}$ is stopping potential) $(\text{ slope })_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{e}} Likewise, \mathrm{hv}=\mathrm{hv}_{0}+\mathrm{K}_{\max }\text{ or } \quad \mathrm{K}_{\max }=\mathrm{h} \mathrm{v}-\mathrm{h} \mathrm{v}_{0} Thus, slope of $ K_{\max }$ vs $v$ is $($\text{ slope })_{2}=\mathrm{h} \therefore \frac{(\text{ slope })_{2}}{(\text{ slope })_{1}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{h} / \mathrm{e}}=\mathrm{e}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A certain metal when irradiated by light $(r=3.2 \times10^{16} \mathrm{~Hz}$ ) emits photoelectrons with twice kinetic energy as did photoelectrons when the same metal is irradiated by light $\left(r=2.0 \times 10^{16} \mathrm{~Hz}\right)$. The $v_{0}$ of metal is
questions.solution: $(\mathrm{KE})_{1}=\mathrm{hv}_{1}-\mathrm{hv}_{0}(\mathrm{KE})_{2}=\mathrm{hv}_{2}-\mathrm{hv}_{0}\begin{array}{ll}\text{ As, } & (\mathrm{KE})_{1}^{2}=2 \times(\mathrm{KE})_{2} \\ \therefore & \mathrm{hv}_{1}-\mathrm{hv}_{0}=2\left(\mathrm{hv}_{2}-\mathrm{hv}_{0}\right) \\ \text{ or, } & \mathrm{hv}_{0}=2 \mathrm{ h} \mathrm{v}_{2}-\mathrm{hv}_{1} \\ \text{ or, } & \mathrm{v}_{0}=2 \mathrm{v}_{2}-\mathrm{v}_{1} \\ & =2 \times\left(2 \times 10^{16}\right)-\left(3.2 \times 10^{16}\right) \\ & =0.8 \times 10^{16} \mathrm{ Hz}=8 \times 10^{15} \mathrm{ Hz}\end{array}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the degeneracy of the level of H-atom that has energy $\left(-\frac{R_{H}}{9}\right)$ ?
questions.solution:
Energy of the electron in the nth orbit in terms of $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is
$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{n}}=-\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}} \mathrmZ^{2}}{\mathrmn^{2}}$
where, $Z=$ atomic number, $n^{2}=$ degeneracy
For $\mathrm{H}$-atom, $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{n}}=-\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}(1)^{2}}{\mathrmn^{2}}-\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}}{9}=-\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}}{\mathrmn^{2}}\therefore \mathrmn^{2}=9$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The wavelengths of two photons are $2000 Å$ and $4000 Å$ respectively. What is the ratio of their energies?
questions.solution: $\begin{array}{l} \quad \mathrm{E}_{1}=\mathrm{h} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{c}}{\lambda_{1}}; \quad \mathrm{E}_{2}=\mathrm{h} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{c}}{\lambda_{2}}\\ \frac{\mathrm{E}_{1}}{\mathrm{E}_{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda_{1}} \times \frac{\lambda_{2}}{\mathrm{hc}}=\frac{\lambda_{2}}{\lambda_{1}}=\frac{4000}{2000}=2 \end{array}$

questions.q: The values of Planck's constant is $6.63 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}$. The velocity of light is $3.0 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{ m} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$. Which value is closest to the wavelength in nanometres of a quantum of light with frequency of $8 \times 10^{15}\mathrms^{-1} ?$
questions.solution: $\mathrm{E}=\mathrm{h} \mathrm{v}=\frac{\mathrm{ch}}{\lambda} ;$ and $\mathrm{v}=\frac{\mathrm{c}}{\lambda}8 \times 10^{15}=\frac{3.0 \times 10^{8}}{\lambda}\begin{aligned} \therefore \lambda &=\frac{3.0 \times 10^{8}}{8 \times 10^{15}}=0.37 \times 10^{-7} \\ &=37.5 \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{ m}=4 \times 10^{1} \mathrm{ nm} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The uncertainty in position and velocity of a particle are $10^{-10} \mathrm{ m}$ and $5.27 \times 10^{-24} \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$ respectively. Calculate the mass of the particle is $(\mathrm{h}=6.625 \times\left.10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}\right)-$
questions.solution: According to Heisenberg's uncertainty principle, $\Delta \mathrm{x} \cdot \mathrm{m} \Delta \mathrm{v}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{4 \pi}$ or $\mathrm{m}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{4 \pi \Delta \mathrm{x}. \Delta \mathrm{v}} \begin{array}{c} =\frac{6.625 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}}{4 \times 3.143 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{ m} \times 5.27 \times 10^{-24} \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}}\\ \because\left[\mathrm{J}=\mathrm{Kgm}^{2} \mathrm{ s}^{2}\right]\\ =0.099 \mathrm{ kg} \end{array}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The magnetic moment of a salt containing $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ ion is
questions.solution:
Magnetic moment of a salt depends upon the number of unpaired d-electrons. In $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ salt configuration of cation is $4 \mathrm{ s}^{0} 3 $$\mathrm{ d}^{10}$$. Hence total no. of unpaired electron, $$\mathrm{n}$$ is zero. So magnetic moment i.e.
$$\text{ B.M. }=$\sqrt{$\mathrm{n}$($\mathrm{n}+$2)}=0
